intent: New style-reference variants, transparent modular sprite sheets

variants.name: 큰 키캡형
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: transparent modular 2D pixel-art keyboard castle wall sprite sheet for Unity, a constrained Jump King-style platformer on an XP-blue-sky background.
Input images: first image is ONLY a visual style/material reference, not an image to copy. Second image is ONLY the existing player sprite for coarse pixel density and scale; do not draw the player.
Create a NEW design. Strict side-on orthographic game sprites, no perspective or 3D render. Large, deliberately visible square pixels like low-resolution 1990s/2000s game art. Think a logical 256x256 pixel atlas scaled up 4x with nearest-neighbor: sparse flat color clusters, hard staircase edges, 1-2 logical pixel charcoal outlines, at most 3 tones per material, no antialiasing, no blur or gradients. Each keycap about half of the player's visible body height.
OUTPUT: square 1024x1024 RGBA image on genuinely transparent background, not black, not a checkerboard drawn into the art. EXACTLY 8 separate wall modules in a rigid 4-column x 2-row grid of equal 256x512 cells, no labels or cell borders.
READING ORDER: top row = LEFT-wall TOP CAP, LEFT-wall REPEAT MIDDLE, LEFT-wall BOTTOM FOOT, LEFT-wall BROKEN OPENING MIDDLE. Bottom row = matching RIGHT-wall TOP CAP, RIGHT-wall REPEAT MIDDLE, RIGHT-wall BOTTOM FOOT, RIGHT-wall BROKEN OPENING MIDDLE.
Functional orientation: left wall's outer spine is on its LEFT and protruding keys/ledges face RIGHT into the level. Right wall is the counterpart with outer spine RIGHT, key faces/ledges facing LEFT.
Modularity is critical: all left modules keep the same vertical body width and horizontal alignment within their cells; all right modules keep the exact mirrored alignment. Logical cell is 64x128. Left spine/body occupies x=14..42, right spine/body x=22..50; key ledges may extend toward the level. Middle modules reach the absolute TOP and BOTTOM edges of their cells with identical flat connector cross-sections; DO NOT cap off repeat tiles, DO NOT leave padding at their splice ends. Top cap has a closed ornamental top but an open matching bottom connector. Bottom foot has a matching open top connector and a closed flat bottom. Spines and cable connectors must align when TOP + MIDDLE + MIDDLE + FOOT are stacked with no scaling.
Broken opening modules retain the SAME top and bottom connectors, but their middle has a conspicuous fully transparent pass-through gap at least 40 logical pixels tall. Fractured keycaps and clipped wire ends surround the hole; no cable runs across and blocks the empty central opening.
Visual subject: computer keyboard keycaps stacked as castle masonry, dark keyboard chassis as the outer structural spine, a few small switches/vents/circuit details. Tiny + or simple dash key markings only, no readable text, logos, letters or labels.
No grass, soil, vines, rocks, sky, scenery, background, characters, floor line, lighting glow, soft shadows or decorative mockup. These are isolated coarse-pixel game wall building blocks, not a presentation poster.

STYLE A — CHUNKY KEYCAP MASONRY. Warm ivory square keycaps are the main large bricks, 3-4 large caps per module; almost-black navy chassis, single bright burnt-orange angular cable on outer edge, a rare one-pixel lime status light. Broad, readable silhouettes and simple bevel highlights matching the supplied reference's material mood. Top and foot each have one longer inward-projecting spacebar ledge. Avoid over-detailing.

STYLE B — SLIM KEYBOARD TOWER FRAME. Keep the reference palette of pale ivory, cool charcoal and burnt orange. The structure is narrower and orderly: vertical metal rail, alternating narrow rectangular modifier keycaps and occasional small square keys, inset switch sockets, a neatly routed orange cable with short stepped joints. Fewer keycaps than the reference and more negative space between them, readable coarse pixels. Top and bottom use restrained short Enter-key brackets, rather than massive platforms. Broken module is a deliberately missing rectangular wall bay with ripped chassis edges. Keep all splice geometry and orientation specifications.

STYLE C — HEAVY RUINED KEYBOARD RAMPART. Use the same ivory/charcoal/orange palette, but arrange staggered square and wide rectangular keycaps as thick castle brickwork, with only a few large cracks, exposed dark key-switch cavities and short broken orange circuit traces. Thick squared silhouette, not organic stone: every brick must still look unmistakably like a keyboard key. Top is a simple stepped keycap battlement and foot a broad chassis plinth. The repeated middle remains structurally solid and repeatable; the broken opening is a large jagged arch-like breach through the wall center, with readable completely empty transparent space, not a dark filled hole. Big chunky pixel clusters, no gritty noise.
